reason: E1 directly supports that HCP elements lower dislocation core energy and alter slip behavior in RHEAs, but it compares TiZrHfNbTa (multiple HCP elements) to VNbMoTaW, not Ti addition to NbMoTaW. E2 and E3 only confirm NbMoTaW's poor ductility and high-temperature strength, providing no evidence for Ti's effect on ductility, irradiation resistance, or phase stability in this system. The irradiation-resistance premise is entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: HCP elements in RHEAs lower dislocation core energy and increase lattice distortion, enhancing ductility
Ti addition will promote additional slip systems at room temperature in NbMoTaW
Increased atomic-level heterogeneity from Ti promotes defect recombination and irradiation resistance
BCC phase stability is maintained up to 1600 °C with modest Ti addition
Ti-modified alloy will show lower irradiation-induced defect accumulation than pure NbMoTaW
